title: Taiwan Approves New Plan for Dementia Care
summaryZh: 行政院通過失智症防治照護3.0計畫，訂2035年「888」目標。
summaryHi: ताइवान ने डिमेंशिया देखभाल की नई योजना मंज़ूर की, 2035 तक '888' लक्ष्य।
summaryEs: Taiwán aprueba un nuevo plan contra la demencia con metas del 80% para 2035.
summaryJa: 台湾行政院が認知症対策3.0を承認、2035年に「888」目標を掲げる。
summaryKo: 대만 행정원이 2035년 '888' 목표의 새 치매 돌봄 계획을 승인했다.
summaryEn: Taiwan approved a new dementia plan with 80% targets for 2035.
paragraphs: Taiwan's Cabinet on Thursday approved an upgraded national strategy for preventing and treating dementia, setting what officials call the "888" targets for 2035. The Dementia Prevention and Care Policy and Action Plan 3.0, drafted by the Ministry of Health and Welfare, has been folded into the government's broader Long-Term Care Plan 3.0.

Under the plan, the government aims to diagnose 80% of dementia cases accurately, provide services to 80% of people living with the condition, and ensure that 80% of staff in designated organisations have a good understanding of the disease. The new goals build on the "777" benchmarks, which Taiwan met in 2025.

Roughly 400,000 older adults in Taiwan have dementia, along with about 10,000 people with young-onset dementia. Deputy Health Minister Lue Jen-der said cases among younger people were increasing, and for the first time the plan includes people under 50 with the condition. The health ministry will cooperate with the Ministry of Labor to help at least 665 of them remain in or return to employment.

The plan also calls for more integrated care centres, community service sites and caregiver support hubs, as well as 4,000 dedicated dementia beds. Long-term care services are expected to reach 420,000 people. Premier Cho Jung-tai asked the ministry to focus on prevention, early screening and counselling, while officials said they would consider whether national health insurance should cover dementia drugs.
Taiwan has a new plan to help people with dementia. Dementia is an illness of the brain. People with it often forget things. The Cabinet said yes to the plan on Thursday.
About 400,000 older people in Taiwan have dementia. About 10,000 younger people have it too. The number of young people with the illness is going up.

The plan has three big goals for 2035. Doctors should find the illness correctly in 80% of cases. 80% of people with dementia should get help. And 80% of workers in some places should understand the illness.
Taiwan will also open more care centres and add 4,000 special beds. The government wants to help young people with dementia keep their jobs.
Taiwan's Cabinet approved a new national plan for dementia on Thursday. The Ministry of Health and Welfare wrote the plan, and it is now part of the country's wider long-term care programme.

Around 400,000 older adults in Taiwan live with dementia, a brain illness that affects memory and thinking. About 10,000 people have young-onset dementia, which starts before old age. Deputy Health Minister Lue Jen-der said the number of younger patients is rising.

The plan sets three targets for 2035, often called the "888" goals. It wants 80% of cases to be diagnosed correctly, 80% of patients to receive services, and 80% of staff in certain workplaces to understand the illness well. These goals follow the "777" targets that Taiwan reached in 2025.
For the first time, the plan also covers younger people with the condition. The health ministry will work with the Ministry of Labor so that at least 665 of them can keep working or go back to work.

By 2035, Taiwan plans to have 153 special dementia care centres, 628 community service sites and 4,000 dementia care beds. The ministry will also study whether national health insurance should pay for dementia medicines.

Taiwan's Cabinet on Thursday approved an upgraded national strategy for preventing and treating dementia, setting what officials call the "888" targets for 2035. The Dementia Prevention and Care Policy and Action Plan 3.0, drafted by the Ministry of Health and Welfare, has been folded into the government's broader Long-Term Care Plan 3.0.

Under the plan, the government aims to diagnose 80% of dementia cases accurately, provide services to 80% of people living with the condition, and ensure that 80% of staff in designated organisations have a good understanding of the disease. The new goals build on the "777" benchmarks, which Taiwan met in 2025.

Roughly 400,000 older adults in Taiwan have dementia, along with about 10,000 people with young-onset dementia. Deputy Health Minister Lue Jen-der said cases among younger people were increasing, and for the first time the plan includes people under 50 with the condition. The health ministry will cooperate with the Ministry of Labor to help at least 665 of them remain in or return to employment.

The plan also calls for more integrated care centres, community service sites and caregiver support hubs, as well as 4,000 dedicated dementia beds. Long-term care services are expected to reach 420,000 people. Premier Cho Jung-tai asked the ministry to focus on prevention, early screening and counselling, while officials said they would consider whether national health insurance should cover dementia drugs.

Taiwan has unveiled a more ambitious blueprint for tackling dementia, with the Cabinet on Thursday endorsing a plan that aims to raise diagnosis, service coverage and public awareness to 80% by 2035. The strategy, known as the Dementia Prevention and Care Policy and Action Plan 3.0, now sits within the government's overarching long-term care framework.

The so-called "888" targets supersede the "777" benchmarks that Taiwan achieved last year, when more than 70% of people with dementia were diagnosed and receiving services. This time, the ministry wants 80% of staff in designated sectors to possess adequate dementia literacy, reflecting a shift towards prevention and early intervention.

Notably, the plan extends support to people under 50 with young-onset dementia, a group of roughly 10,000 that has often fallen through the cracks. Deputy Health Minister Lue Jen-der said such cases were on the rise, and the ministry intends to work with labour officials so that at least 665 patients can keep or regain their jobs.

On the infrastructure side, the number of integrated dementia care centres is set to grow from 133 to 153, while community service sites will expand to 628 and 4,000 dedicated beds will be added. Officials also pledged to examine whether dementia medication should be reimbursed by National Health Insurance, a move that could ease the financial burden on families caring for an estimated 400,000 older patients.

Taiwan's Cabinet has approved a comprehensive overhaul of its national dementia strategy, committing the government to a set of measurable objectives for 2035. Dubbed the "888" targets, the goals envisage an 80% rate of accurate diagnosis, 80% service coverage and 80% dementia literacy among personnel in designated organisations.

The initiative, formally titled the Dementia Prevention and Care Policy and Action Plan 3.0, has been incorporated into the broader Long-Term Care Plan 3.0. It consolidates the progress made under the previous "777" framework, whose benchmarks were attained in 2025, and is structured around four pillars: prevention, precise diagnosis, enhanced service capacity and the safeguarding of patients' rights.

A significant innovation is the inclusion of individuals under 50 with young-onset dementia, estimated to number around 10,000. Deputy Health Minister Lue Jen-der acknowledged that the prevalence of such cases was increasing, and the health ministry will collaborate with the Ministry of Labor to enable at least 665 of these patients to retain or resume employment.

Capacity will also be expanded considerably, with integrated care centres rising to 153, community sites to 628 and dedicated dementia beds reaching 4,000. Moreover, the ministry has undertaken to assess whether dementia drugs should be covered by National Health Insurance, a decision that could substantially alleviate the financial strain on the families of Taiwan's estimated 400,000 older patients.

note.meaning: 減輕、緩解（痛苦、問題、壓力等）。

noteKo.usage: 타동사로 pain / poverty / pressure 등 부정적 명사를 목적어로 취함. reduce보다 격식적.

inclusion.en: the act of including someone or something
inclusion.ex: The inclusion of children's books made the library popular.
inclusion.ja: 対象に含めること；包含

incorporated.en: included as part of something larger
incorporated.ex: Her ideas were incorporated into the final design.

note.meaning: 被納入、併入（更大的整體之中）。
note.usage: incorporate 的過去分詞，常用被動 be incorporated into / in + 名詞；主動為 incorporate A into B。也可指公司「註冊成立」。

example.en: Students' suggestions were incorporated into the final design.
example.zh: 學生的建議被納入了最終設計之中。

noteHi.meaning: (किसी बड़े हिस्से में) शामिल किया गया, सम्मिलित।
noteHi.usage: incorporate का भूतकृदंत; प्रायः कर्मवाच्य: be incorporated into + संज्ञा। कर्तृवाच्य: incorporate A into B।
noteHi.exampleTr: छात्रों के सुझावों को अंतिम डिज़ाइन में शामिल किया गया।

noteEs.meaning: incorporado, integrado en un conjunto mayor.
noteEs.usage: Participio de incorporate; suele usarse en pasiva: be incorporated into + sustantivo. Activa: incorporate A into B.
noteEs.exampleTr: Las sugerencias de los estudiantes se incorporaron al diseño final.

noteJa.meaning: （より大きな全体に）組み込まれた、盛り込まれた。
noteJa.usage: incorporate の過去分詞。受動態 be incorporated into ～ の形が多い。能動態は incorporate A into B。
noteJa.exampleTr: 学生の提案は最終デザインに盛り込まれた。

noteKo.usage: incorporate의 과거분사. 수동태 be incorporated into + 명사 형태가 흔함. 능동은 incorporate A into B.

noteEn.meaning: included as part of something larger.
noteEn.usage: Past participle of 'incorporate'; often passive: 'be incorporated into + noun'.

increasing.en: becoming larger in number or amount
increasing.ex: The number of tourists is increasing every year.

individuals.ex: Ten individuals signed up for the course.

infrastructure.en: basic systems and structures like roads, railways and buildings
infrastructure.ex: The country spent billions on roads and other infrastructure.

initiative.en: a new plan to solve a problem
initiative.ex: The initiative aims to plant a million trees.

innovation.ex: The biggest innovation is a free bus service.

insurance.en: a system that pays costs such as medical bills
insurance.ex: Health insurance pays for most of her treatment.

integrated.en: combining different parts or services into one; joined together with
integrated.ex: The new station will be integrated with the bus terminal.
integrated.ja: 統合型の；一体化された
integrated.zh: 整合的；（be integrated with）與…相連

intends.en: plans or means to do something
intends.ex: The school intends to hire more teachers.
intends.ja: 〜するつもりだ；予定している

intervention.en: action taken to improve a situation or stop a problem getting worse
intervention.ex: Early intervention can help children with reading problems.

into.en: to the inside of; changing to become something

is.ex: The museum is open every day except Monday.

jen-der.en: given name of Lue Jen-der, deputy health minister

jobs.ex: The new factory will create 500 jobs.

jung-tai.en: given name of Cho Jung-tai, Taiwan's premier

keep.en: to continue to have or do something
keep.ex: He wants to keep his job after the operation.

known.ex: The area is known as the old town.
known.hi: के नाम से जाना जाता है
known.ja: 〜として知られる；〜と呼ばれる

labor.en: work, especially paid work (US spelling; Ministry of Labor)
labor.es: trabajo; (Ministry of Labor) Ministerio de Trabajo
labor.ex: The Ministry of Labor published new rules for workers.

labour.en: work and workers, especially as a government area
labour.ex: Labour officials met business leaders on Tuesday.

last.en: the one before this one (e.g. last year)
last.ex: We went to Japan last summer.

least.ex: You should sleep at least seven hours a night.

literacy.en: knowledge and understanding of a subject
literacy.ex: Digital literacy is an important skill for young workers.

live.en: to have your life; (live with) to have an illness long-term
live.ex: Many people live with back pain for years.
live.ja: 暮らす；（live with）〜を抱えて生きる

living.en: having a life; (living with) having an illness
living.es: que viven; (living with) que viven con
living.ex: Support is available for people living with cancer.
living.ja: 暮らす；（living with）〜を抱えて生きる

long-term.en: lasting or relating to a long period of time
long-term.es: a largo plazo; de larga duración
long-term.ex: Long-term care is needed for many older patients.

lue.en: family name of Taiwan's deputy health minister Lue Jen-der

made.zh: 取得；做出（make 的過去分詞）
made.en: achieved or produced (past participle of make)
made.ex: We have made good progress on the report this week.

measurable.ex: The team set clear, measurable goals for the year.

medication.en: medicine used to treat an illness
medication.ex: She takes medication every morning for her heart.

medicines.ex: Keep all medicines away from small children.

memory.ex: My grandfather's memory is getting worse.

met.en: reached or achieved (a target); past tense of meet
met.ex: The factory met its sales target last month.

minister.en: a senior member of a government who heads a department
minister.ex: The minister answered questions from reporters.

ministry.ex: The ministry released new rules for schools.

more.en: a greater number of; to a greater degree (more easily, more costly)

moreover.en: in addition to what has been said
moreover.ex: The plan is cheap; moreover, it is easy to start.

move.en: an action taken to achieve something (n.); to go from place to place (v.)
move.ex: Cutting bus fares was a popular move.

national.ex: The team won the national championship last year.

new.ex: The city opened a new library downtown.

notably.ja: 特に；注目すべきことに
notably.en: in a way that deserves attention; especially
notably.ex: Notably, the new law also protects part-time workers.

now.ex: The shop is now closed for the holiday.

number.en: an amount of people or things (n.); to add up to (v.)
number.ex: The number of visitors grew every year.

objectives.en: things that you plan to achieve
objectives.ex: The company explained its main objectives for next year.

of.en: belonging to; showing a part or amount

officials.en: people with positions of authority in government
officials.ex: City officials will announce the results tomorrow.

often.ex: We often eat lunch in the park.

old.en: having existed for a long time; of advanced age (old age)
old.ex: The old bridge will be closed next month.

older.ex: Older people may need help with shopping.

on.en: used for days (on Thursday) and states (on the rise, on foot)

open.en: to start a new place or service
open.ex: The bank will open two new branches this year.

organisations.en: groups of people working together for a purpose
organisations.ex: Many organisations offer free training for volunteers.

overarching.ex: Safety is the overarching aim of the new rules.

overhaul.en: a complete review and improvement of a system
overhaul.ex: The tax system needs a complete overhaul.

note.meaning: （制度、政策等的）全面翻修、徹底改革。
note.usage: 可數名詞，常用 a (major / comprehensive) overhaul of + 名詞；也可作動詞 overhaul the system（徹底改革制度）。常見於政策、新聞語境。

example.en: The tax system is in urgent need of an overhaul.

noteHi.meaning: किसी व्यवस्था या नीति का पूर्ण सुधार या नवीनीकरण।
noteHi.usage: संज्ञा: an overhaul of + संज्ञा; क्रिया के रूप में भी: overhaul the system। नीति व समाचार में आम।
noteHi.exampleTr: कर प्रणाली को तत्काल पूर्ण सुधार की आवश्यकता है।

noteEs.meaning: reforma completa o revisión a fondo de un sistema o política.
noteEs.usage: Sustantivo: an overhaul of + sustantivo; también verbo: overhaul the system. Frecuente en política y noticias.
noteEs.exampleTr: El sistema tributario necesita urgentemente una reforma a fondo.

noteJa.meaning: （制度・政策などの）全面的な見直し、抜本的改革。
noteJa.usage: 名詞で an overhaul of ～ の形が多い。動詞 overhaul the system（制度を抜本改革する）も可。政策・報道でよく使う。
noteJa.exampleTr: 税制は早急な抜本的改革を必要としている。

noteKo.usage: 명사로 an overhaul of + 명사 형태가 흔함. 동사 overhaul the system(제도를 전면 개편하다)도 가능. 정책·뉴스에서 자주 쓰임.

noteEn.meaning: a complete change or repair of a system to make it work better.
noteEn.usage: Often 'an overhaul of + noun' ('an overhaul of the strategy'); also a verb: 'overhaul the system'.

part.en: a piece or section of something larger
part.ex: This part of the city is very quiet.

patients.ex: The doctor sees thirty patients a day.

pay.ex: The company will pay for your training.

people.ex: Many people visit the market on Sundays.

personnel.en: the people employed in an organisation
personnel.ex: All hospital personnel must wear name cards.

pillars.en: the main parts that support a plan or idea
pillars.ex: Education and health are the pillars of the policy.

places.ex: There are many places to eat near the station.

plan.en: a set of actions decided on to achieve something
plan.ex: The city has a plan to build more parks.

plans.ex: The school plans to open a new library.

pledged.ex: The mayor pledged to clean up the river.

policy.en: a plan of action adopted by a government
policy.ex: The new policy helps young families buy homes.

possess.en: to have a quality or skill
possess.ex: Few people possess her talent for languages.

precise.ex: We need precise measurements before we cut the wood.

premier.en: the head of the government (in Taiwan, head of the Executive Yuan)
premier.ex: The premier visited the flooded villages.

prevalence.en: how common something is in a population
prevalence.ex: The prevalence of diabetes is rising in cities.

note.meaning: 盛行、普遍程度；（疾病等的）盛行率。
note.usage: 不可數名詞，常用 the prevalence of + 名詞；在醫療、統計中指某族群中患病比例。形容詞 prevalent（普遍的）。

example.en: The prevalence of diabetes has risen sharply among young adults.
example.zh: 糖尿病在年輕成人中的盛行率急遽上升。

noteHi.usage: अगणनीय संज्ञा: the prevalence of + संज्ञा; स्वास्थ्य व आँकड़ों में आम। विशेषण: prevalent।
noteHi.exampleTr: युवा वयस्कों में मधुमेह की व्यापकता तेज़ी से बढ़ी है।

noteEs.meaning: prevalencia; grado en que algo es común o frecuente.
noteEs.usage: Sustantivo incontable: the prevalence of + sustantivo; común en salud y estadística. Adjetivo: prevalent.
noteEs.exampleTr: La prevalencia de la diabetes ha aumentado notablemente entre los adultos jóvenes.

noteJa.meaning: 普及度、広がり；（病気の）有病率。
noteJa.usage: 不可算名詞で the prevalence of ～ の形が多い。医療・統計でよく使う。形容詞は prevalent。
noteJa.exampleTr: 若年成人の間で糖尿病の有病率が急上昇している。

noteKo.usage: 불가산 명사로 the prevalence of + 명사 형태가 흔함. 의료·통계에서 자주 쓰임. 형용사 prevalent.
noteKo.exampleTr: 젊은 성인층에서 당뇨병 유병률이 급격히 증가했다.

noteEn.meaning: how common something is, especially a disease, in a group of people.
noteEn.usage: Uncountable; usually 'the prevalence of + noun'. Common in health and statistics.

preventing.ex: Washing hands helps in preventing disease.

prevention.en: the act of stopping something bad from happening
prevention.ex: Fire prevention is taught in every school.

previous.ex: The previous owner painted the house blue.

programme.en: a planned series of activities or services
programme.ex: The city runs a free health programme for seniors.

progress.ex: The workers made fast progress on the new road.

provide.ex: The hotel will provide free breakfast.

public.ex: Public interest in the election is very high.

raise.en: to increase the level of something
raise.ex: The school wants to raise reading levels.

rate.en: a measure of how often something happens, often a percentage
rate.ex: The success rate of the treatment is high.

reach.en: to get to a number, level or stage
reach.ex: The project should reach its goal next year.

reached.en: achieved; got to (past tense of reach)
reached.ex: The climbers reached the top before noon.

reaching.en: getting to a certain number or level
reaching.ex: Prices are reaching record levels this summer.

receive.ex: All students will receive a free book.

receiving.ex: She is receiving treatment at a local hospital.

reflecting.en: showing or being a sign of something
reflecting.ex: Sales rose, reflecting greater demand for electric cars.

regain.en: to get something back after losing it
regain.ex: He worked hard to regain his health.

reimbursed.ja: 払い戻される；給付される
reimbursed.en: paid back for money spent; covered by insurance
reimbursed.ex: Your travel costs will be reimbursed by the company.

remain.ja: とどまる；〜のままである
remain.en: to stay in the same place or condition
remain.ex: Please remain in your seats until the bus stops.

resume.en: to start again after a pause
resume.ex: Classes will resume after the holiday.

retain.ex: The firm wants to retain its best workers.

return.ex: She will return to work after the baby is born.

rights.en: things people are morally or legally allowed to have
rights.ex: The law protects the rights of workers.

rise.ex: Crime in the area is on the rise.

roughly.ex: The trip takes roughly two hours by car.

safeguarding.ex: The safeguarding of children is everyone's job.

note.meaning: 保障、維護、保護（權益、安全等）。
note.usage: safeguard 的動名詞／名詞用法，常用 the safeguarding of + 名詞（rights / interests）；動詞 safeguard sth (against / from sth)。名詞 safeguard 亦指「保護措施」。

example.en: Safeguarding personal data has become a priority for banks.
example.zh: 保障個人資料已成為銀行的首要任務。

noteHi.meaning: (अधिकारों, हितों आदि की) रक्षा या सुरक्षा करना।
noteHi.usage: safeguard का V-ing / संज्ञा रूप: the safeguarding of rights। क्रिया: safeguard sth against sth।
noteHi.exampleTr: व्यक्तिगत डेटा की सुरक्षा बैंकों की प्राथमिकता बन गई है।

noteEs.usage: Forma -ing de safeguard: the safeguarding of rights. Verbo: safeguard sth against sth.
noteEs.exampleTr: La protección de los datos personales se ha convertido en una prioridad para los bancos.

noteJa.meaning: （権利・利益・安全などを）守ること、保護。
noteJa.usage: safeguard の動名詞。the safeguarding of rights の形が多い。動詞は safeguard ～ against ...。
noteJa.exampleTr: 個人データの保護は銀行にとって最優先事項となった。

noteKo.usage: safeguard의 동명사형. the safeguarding of rights 형태가 흔함. 동사 safeguard ~ against ....
noteKo.exampleTr: 개인정보 보호는 은행들의 최우선 과제가 되었다.

noteEn.meaning: protecting something, such as rights or safety, from harm.
noteEn.usage: -ing form of 'safeguard'; often 'the safeguarding of + noun'.

said.en: stated (past tense of say); (said yes = agreed)
said.ex: The teacher said the test was next week.

screening.en: medical tests to find a disease early
screening.ex: Free cancer screening is offered to adults over fifty.

sectors.en: parts of an economy or society
sectors.ex: Jobs grew in the health and education sectors.

service.en: help or work provided for people
service.ex: The village has a new bus service.

services.en: kinds of help provided for people
services.ex: The clinic offers free services to older people.

set.zh: 預定的（set to）；一組（a set of）
set.en: planned or expected (set to); a group of things (a set of)
set.ex: Prices are set to rise next month.

sets.en: decides or fixes (a goal or rule)
sets.ex: The school sets clear rules for every class.

setting.ex: She is setting new goals for the team.

shift.en: a change in direction or focus
shift.ex: There has been a shift towards online shopping.

should.en: used to say what is right or expected
should.ex: You should drink more water every day.

side.en: one part or aspect of a situation
side.ex: On the money side, the plan looks good.

significant.ex: This is a significant step for the company.

sites.en: places used for a service; places with old remains
sites.ex: Workers found several ancient sites near the river.

sits.en: is placed or included within something
sits.ex: The new office sits within the main building.

so-called.ex: The so-called smart city opened last year.

special.ex: The hospital has a special room for children.

staff.en: the people who work for an organisation
staff.ex: All staff must wear a name card.

starts.ex: The film starts at seven tonight.

strain.en: pressure or difficulty caused by too much demand
strain.ex: High rent puts a strain on young families.

strategy.en: a plan to achieve a goal
strategy.ex: The company needs a new sales strategy.

structured.ex: The course is structured around five topics.

study.ex: The council will study the new proposal.

substantially.ex: Prices have risen substantially since last year.

note.usage: 副詞，修飾動詞或比較級（substantially improve / substantially higher）；比 greatly 正式，學術寫作常用。形容詞 substantial。

example.en: Public transport use has increased substantially since fares were cut.
example.zh: 自票價調降以來，大眾運輸使用量大幅增加。

noteHi.meaning: काफ़ी हद तक; उल्लेखनीय रूप से।
noteHi.usage: क्रियाविशेषण; क्रिया या तुलनात्मक के साथ (substantially improve / higher)। greatly से अधिक औपचारिक।
noteHi.exampleTr: किराया घटने के बाद से सार्वजनिक परिवहन का उपयोग काफ़ी बढ़ा है।

noteEs.usage: Adverbio que modifica verbos o comparativos (substantially improve / higher). Más formal que greatly.
noteEs.exampleTr: El uso del transporte público ha aumentado considerablemente desde que se rebajaron las tarifas.

noteJa.usage: 副詞で動詞や比較級を修飾する（substantially improve / higher）。greatly より硬く、論文でよく使う。
noteJa.exampleTr: 運賃が引き下げられて以来、公共交通の利用は大幅に増えた。

noteKo.usage: 부사로 동사나 비교급을 수식(substantially improve / higher). greatly보다 격식적이며 학술 글에서 흔함.
noteKo.exampleTr: 요금 인하 이후 대중교통 이용이 대폭 늘었다.

noteEn.usage: Used with verbs or comparatives ('substantially improve', 'substantially higher'); formal.

supersede.en: take the place of something older
supersede.ex: New rules will supersede the old ones.

support.ex: Parents need support during the first months.

tackling.ex: The city is tackling air pollution.

taiwan.en: an island country in East Asia

targets.ex: The team met all its sales targets.

these.en: the ones here or just mentioned

thinking.en: the use of the mind to form ideas

this.en: the one here or just mentioned

through.en: from one side to the other; (fall through the cracks) be missed

thursday.ex: The meeting is on Thursday afternoon.

time.ex: It was my first time on a plane.

titled.en: given a particular name or title
titled.ex: Her new book is titled Home Again.

treating.en: giving medical care for an illness
treating.ex: Doctors are treating the patient at home.

under.en: according to (under the plan); less than (under 50); below

understand.en: know the meaning or nature of
understand.ex: Do you understand the new rules?

understanding.ex: She has a good understanding of maths.

undertaken.en: promised or agreed to do something
undertaken.ex: The council has undertaken to repair the road.

note.meaning: （正式）承諾、保證要做；著手進行、承擔。
note.usage: undertake 的過去分詞（undertake-undertook-undertaken）。undertake to V 表「承諾去做」，文中 has undertaken to assess 即此義；undertake a task / study 表「著手進行」。

example.en: The council has undertaken to repair the bridge by spring.
example.zh: 市議會已承諾在春天前修好這座橋。

noteHi.meaning: (औपचारिक रूप से) कुछ करने का वचन देना; कोई कार्य शुरू करना या अपने ज़िम्मे लेना।
noteHi.usage: undertake का भूतकृदंत। undertake to + क्रिया = करने का वचन देना; undertake a task/study = कार्य आरंभ करना।
noteHi.exampleTr: परिषद ने वसंत तक पुल की मरम्मत करने का वचन दिया है।

noteEs.meaning: comprometido (a hacer algo); emprendido, llevado a cabo.
noteEs.usage: Participio de undertake. undertake to + verbo = comprometerse a; undertake a task/study = emprender una tarea.
noteEs.exampleTr: El ayuntamiento se ha comprometido a reparar el puente antes de la primavera.

noteJa.meaning: （正式に）～することを約束した；（仕事などに）着手した、引き受けた。
noteJa.usage: undertake の過去分詞。undertake to do は「～すると約束する」、undertake a task/study は「着手する」。
noteJa.exampleTr: 市議会は春までに橋を修理すると約束した。

noteKo.usage: undertake의 과거분사. undertake to do는 '~하기로 약속하다', undertake a task/study는 '착수하다'.

noteEn.meaning: promised formally to do something; also started or taken on a task.
noteEn.usage: Past participle of 'undertake'. 'Undertake to do' = promise to do; 'undertake a study' = carry it out.

unveiled.en: showed or announced publicly for the first time
unveiled.ex: The company unveiled its new phone today.

up.en: to a higher level (go up); (free up) make available
up.ex: Food prices went up again this month.

upgraded.ex: We tested the upgraded software yesterday.

was.ex: The station was very busy yesterday.

welfare.en: help and care for people's health and comfort
welfare.ex: The charity works for child welfare.

well.en: in a good or thorough way; (as well as) and also
well.ex: He knows the city very well.

were.ex: The roads were empty on Sunday.

whether.en: used to express a choice (if or not)

which.en: used to add information about a thing

while.en: and at the same time; whereas

wider.ex: This is part of a wider problem.

will.en: used to talk about the future
will.ex: The new bridge will open next year.

work.en: do a job or act together (v.); a job or a project (n.)
work.ex: Our teams work together on many projects.

workers.ex: The workers finished the bridge early.

working.ex: He kept working after he turned seventy.

workplaces.ex: Many workplaces now allow working from home.

would.en: used to talk about a future from the past
would.ex: She said she would call me later.

wrote.ex: My father wrote a letter to the mayor.

year.ex: Last year we moved to Tainan.

yes.ex: The teacher said yes to our idea.

young-onset.hi: कम उम्र में शुरू होने वाला
young-onset.en: starting at a younger age than usual
young-onset.ex: He was diagnosed with young-onset dementia at 45.
